notes: Line forms: {n} Feyre's narration, first person past tense, shown in italics; {s,e,t} a line spoken aloud (speaker, portrait expression, text); {hint} a game tip on its own card; {choices:[{t,goto,do}]}; {do:[actions]}; {goto}. Any line or choice may carry if_flag, if_not_flag, if_item, if_not_item or if_chapter. Wording is written for the game; the few short book lines kept are listed in quotes.json.

lines.n: His head snapped round. Yellow eyes found mine through the thorns.

lines.hint: Watch his eyes. When they flare and he crouches low, he's about to lunge. Step out of the way, then hit back while he recovers.

lines.n: He came out of the brush in a blur of grey and black and white. The doe never stood a chance.

lines.t: No. That was a week of food.

lines.n: The ash arrow struck deep in his side, and I'd have sworn the ground shuddered under me.
He whirled toward the thicket with a snarl that rattled my teeth.
He stumbled mid-stride, and snarled at the shaft in his flank.
Where the arrow had gone in, the wound wasn't closing.

lines.t: So the stories were true. Ash.

lines.n: His legs twitched once. A low whine, and then nothing.
I waited until that great coat of charcoal and ivory had stopped rising and falling.

lines.t: Just a wolf. A very large one.

lines.n: It took a long time with a hunting knife and fingers I could barely feel. I worked the pelt free, rolled it tight and lashed it to my pack.

lines.t: Far too big for a wolf. Far too heavy.

lines.n: The doe hadn't run. Fear had rooted her where she stood.
I made it quick. She deserved that much.
What the wolf had left of her was torn and ruined. Still meat. Still a hide, of a sort.
I hoisted her across my shoulders. She weighed more than she looked, and she looked like nothing at all.
